task.question: On what date did Ukraine boycott the closing ceremony of the 2026 Winter Paralympics?
task.evidence: 15 March – Ukraine boycotts the closing ceremony of the 2026 Winter Paralympics in Italy in protest over Russian athletes being allowed to compete under the Russian flag after the lifting of sanctions imposed over the Russian invasion in 2022.

Ukraine Boycotts Paralympics Closing Ceremony Over Russian Presence | Winter Paralympics 2026 - Archysport Skip to content Menu Home badminton baseball basketball football Golf judo Nfl Sport news Tennis Ukraine Boycotts Paralympics Closing Ceremony Over Russian Presence | Winter Paralympics 2026 March 14, 2026 by Editor-in-Chief Cortina d’Ampezzo, Italy – The Ukrainian Paralympic team will not participate in the closing ceremony of the Winter Paralympics in Cortina d’Ampezzo on Sunday, March 15, 2026, in protest against the International Paralympic Committee’s (IPC) decision to allow Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete under their own flags. The move escalates a growing international outcry over the inclusion of athletes from nations involved in the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. Valeriy Sushkevych, President of the National Paralympic Committee of Ukraine, confirmed the boycott to the German Press Agency (dpa) on Saturday. “No, never,” Sushkevych stated when asked about Ukrainian participation in the ceremony. “The flag of a state murderer will be raised there.” He went on to call these Paralympic Games “the worst in history.” Sushkevych’s condemnation centers on what he perceives as a betrayal by the IPC, a stark contrast to the ban imposed on Russian and Belarusian national symbols at the 2022 Winter Paralympics in Beijing following Russia’s initial invasion of Ukraine. The decision to lift that ban for the Milan-Cortina Games has sparked widespread criticism and prompted several nations to protest. The Ukrainian Paralympic chief accused Russian Paralympians of openly supporting Russian President Vladimir Putin, who has been waging war against Ukraine for over four years. He specifically pointed to instances of Russian gold medalists dedicating their victories to Putin, rather than their country or its people. “That shows that the athletes are not only representing their country, but also terrorism, war and military attacks. The ceremony is scheduled for 9:30 p.m. Kyiv time at the Olympic Ice Stadium in Cortina d'Ampezzo. No Ukrainian delegation will attend. Before the final day of competition, Ukrainian para cross-country skier Hryhorii Vovchynskyi told Suspilne Sport that the team would decide on the boycott at a general meeting. He expressed strong opposition to competing alongside athletes from Russia and Belarus while the war continues in Ukraine.
